fact_check_rounds.label: Round 1: the 40 profiled plants (after the parallel list audit)
Round 2: confirming round, all 47 profiled plants, checkers rotated (after the sweep)
Round 3: the 21 profiles added in the last waves (profilers G, H, I and J)
Round 4: the two OSHA-closure plants profiled into the top 40 after the R3 audit (Kafka Mosinee, Laidig Mishawaka)
Round 6: line check of all 71 profiled plants' lines after constrained rewriting (validator-gated), three checkers who did not write them
Targeted sweep, not a sample: 64 rows flagged by tools/sweep_company_level.py because they looked company-level (rate not comparable with the sampled rounds)
Cross-vertical checks (state air permits, job-board dates, OSHA headcounts, profiles of OSHA top-40 entrants): rows for this vertical's plants
Base-record samples: 25 closure-3 base records, and 25 of the 51 records added on 2026-11-17 by closure 5 and the R3 miss verification (reported separately; not a profile round)

miss_rate.value: 15/94 = 16.0% (blind audit R3, verified, written boundary rule); 20.2-21.8% if a stated skid-steer line kept a plant in; up to 25.5% if the 12 unverified candidates are real
miss_rate.note: Third blind audit (two auditors, new methods, 2026-11-17) after closure pass 5 (OSHA 300A establishments verified by a sourced in-definition product at the site). Miss rate = verified misses / (included plants found + verified misses), as in R2; excluded plants found leave the count; plants in the ledger under another city or name count as found after verification; all 85 matched pairs were read (one wrong pair, Builtrite to LaBounty, counted as a miss). R3-C: 4 misses (+ Builtrite); R3-D: 10. All verified misses are now base records; merging them does not lower the measured rate.
history: 16.0% verified (Nov 17, blind audit R3 after the OSHA closure)

known_limits: Miss rate (third blind audit, R3, two auditors with new methods): 15/94 = 16.0% under the written boundary rule (the core welded product decides; lifting-led and tractor-led attachment makers go to v-cranes-lifting and v-agricultural-equipment, applied alike to found plants and misses; compact and skid-steer attachment makers count, as in R2). If any stated skid-steer or excavator line kept a plant in mining, it would be 20/99 = 20.2% (22/101 = 21.8% with MDS and Panova), over the 20% bar. Builtrite (Two Harbors MN) is counted as a miss unverified; Panova was never verified. If all 12 unverifiable leads were real misses: 27/106 = 25.5%. Neither auditor reached a dry point (both stopped at their search budgets), and both wrote files into a scratchpad they were told not to open (they read nothing there). R2 measured 27.6% and the first audit 30.2%.

Closure 5 (OSHA 300A establishments in NAICS 333120, 333131, 333922, 332313; 776 screened) added 37 records (34 base, 2 profiled, 1 excluded); R3 verification added 20 (15 base, 5 excluded to other verticals). 19 of those closure base records and 11 of the audit-verified base records have prospect_test unknown (an in-definition product made at the site is stated, welding is not); held as base (Caterpillar Clayton precedent). A seeded sample of 25 of the 51 non-excluded records added on 2026-11-17 found 4/300 = 1.3% (CS closure-5 sample).

Opening lines and bottleneck guesses of all 70 profiled plants were rebuilt under constrained composition and gated by tools/validate_lines.py; round 6 line check 2/134 = 1.5% (1/100 on High and Medium). Five bottleneck guesses are 'unknown' (Low 4, Medium 1). Virnig Rice's opening line and the Rockland, Virnig fallbacks were written by checkers and checked by another (R9).

Postings re-read on 2026-11-17 moved labor at Rockland Bedford (73 -> 65, closed posting), Virnig Rice (58 -> 46, closed), Mellott Warfordsburg (60 -> 52, a batch re-list read as a standing ad), J.H. Fletcher (48 -> 40, a re-post stamp of a 2025 requisition) and Kafka Mosinee (55 -> 43, careers-page ad with no apply flow of its own). IROCK keeps labor 12 on a blanket 'send applications to' instruction (36 Low if a per-role instruction were required); Werk-Brau's 60+ days rests on job-ID order (inferred under 12 months).
Standard Iron's two Hartford plants are held as base: their only welder posting names both addresses and never says which one hires.

Cross-vertical checks (round 8, incl. the targeted closeout check) for mining's plants: 22/175 = 12.6%, or 8/89 = 9.0% without Standard Iron Hartford's two records (brand-level rows, retagged). The company-level sweep (round 7, targeted) retagged 41 rows; it sees only pages cited by two or more plants.

The two verified misses that ranked in the top 40 with counted postings were profiled afterwards: Fecon, Lebanon OH, 76 High (three undated welder postings open at once; boundary, forestry mulching attachments) and General Steel & Supply (Fisher Industries), Dickinson ND, 28 Low under the strict campus rule (75 High if a 2021 source placing both fabrication facilities on its Energy Drive campus is accepted). The top 40 is now fully profiled.

About 155 EPA registry rows and named leads from closure remain unverified, plus 15 re-audit candidates and leads such as Tricon's other plants, Power Curbers' Cedar Falls and McHenry plants, HitchDoc's Kwik-Way Sioux Falls plant and Amerequip's New Holstein plants.

Brookville Equipment, Brookville PA scores 63 Medium under the written campus rule: the flat car's size is a company-level fact and a second Brookville site (service and rebuilds) is 1.3 km away. If the rebuild shop is ruled not a production site, it is 83 High.

Material scores 0 on 59 of 68 profiled plants: mining and construction sources rarely state a welded part's size or weight, and payloads, bucket capacities and machine classes do not count as part sizes.

Paladin Dexter MI is profiled as a boundary plant: no Paladin page says what it builds, and EPA's facility name (Sweepster-Harley Attachments) points to sweeper and broom attachments, which would exclude it under the M-B New Holstein ruling.
Auditor B could see file names (not contents) in the shared scratchpad during the re-audit, so its blindness is slightly weaker than auditor A's.
